Choose a database for your application

Use an inventory app to see how query patterns, transaction needs, and reporting shape the database choice.

Open interactive lesson

On this page

  • Start with what the app must do
  • Match the data model to the queries
  • Compare operational queries and analytics
  • Official references

Start with what the app must do

Write down the queries and updates the app needs. Estimate how often they run and what the app must guarantee when changes happen together.

-- Can warehouse 3 fulfill a request for 5 units of product 42?
SELECT quantity
FROM stock_balances
WHERE warehouse_id = 3
  AND product_id = 42
  AND quantity >= 5;
Queries
Find a product by SKU. Show stock by warehouse. Read movement history for the last month.
Transactions
When moving stock, record the movement and update both warehouse balances together.
Operational requirements
Estimate reads and writes, acceptable response times, and data growth. Decide who can run backups and test restores.

Match the data model to the queries

Start with the hardest operation on that list. For inventory, one example is transferring stock while keeping the movement record and both balances in sync. A relational database is a reasonable starting point for inventory because the application relates products, warehouses, stock balances, and movement records and needs consistent updates. Add another store when you have a specific access pattern or performance requirement to satisfy.

-- Assume both balance rows exist and quantity has CHECK (quantity >= 0).
BEGIN;

UPDATE stock_balances SET quantity = quantity - 5
WHERE warehouse_id = 3 AND product_id = 42;

UPDATE stock_balances SET quantity = quantity + 5
WHERE warehouse_id = 4 AND product_id = 42;

INSERT INTO stock_movements
  (product_id, from_warehouse_id, to_warehouse_id, quantity)
VALUES (42, 3, 4, 5);

COMMIT;
Relational · PostgreSQL / MySQL
Keep products, warehouse balances, and stock movements in linked tables.
Document · MongoDB
A catalog that usually reads an entire product with its category-specific attributes can represent each product as a document.
Key-value · Redis
Cache a frequently read product listing under a known key. Set an expiry and refresh or remove the cached entry after catalog changes as needed.
Graph · Neo4j
A graph suits queries that follow several links, such as tracing dependencies between parts.
Wide-column · Cassandra
Use a known partition-key-based access pattern, such as retrieving movement events by warehouse and day.

Compare operational queries and analytics

The same inventory app may record a transfer in the morning and summarize months of transfers in an afternoon report. Those two jobs read and write data in different ways. OLTP and OLAP describe workloads. Measure the cost of reports on the operational database before introducing a separate analytical store.

-- OLTP: read one balance while taking an order.
SELECT quantity FROM stock_balances
WHERE warehouse_id = 3 AND product_id = 42;

-- OLAP: summarize movements across several months.
SELECT date_trunc('month', moved_at) AS month, SUM(quantity) AS units_moved
FROM stock_movements
WHERE moved_at >= DATE '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month;
OLTP
Record a stock transfer as the user submits it and update the affected balances.
OLAP
Summarize months of movements across products and warehouses to see stock trends. Many small teams can start with SQL reports in their relational database and move heavier reporting elsewhere as it grows.
